query: For additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy with an fcc matrix, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs degradation during elevated-temperature exposure to oxidizing or reducing gases and why catastrophic failure may occur? Specify a controlled change that would reveal the governing behavior, predicted observations relative to the starting-state baseline, applicable exposure boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a clear falsification criterion.

generation.material_initial_state: Arc-melted, polished, nominally equiatomic AlCrCoFeNi high-entropy alloy in the as-cast state; XRD showed a dual-phase BCC (~79%) and ordered B2 (~21%) structure with a maze-like spinodally decomposed microstructure. EDS measured ~17.26 at.% Al rather than the nominal 20 at.%.
generation.intervention: The alloy was heated in situ from room temperature to 1100 °C under either low-oxygen/vacuum or atmospheric-air conditions while HTXRD tracked phase and oxide evolution; equilibrium phase and oxide formation were also calculated with Thermo-Calc/CALPHAD using TCHEA7 and TCNi11 databases.
generation.conditions: Heating proceeded at 10 °C/min in 50 °C increments, with a 5 min hold at each setpoint and XRD scans over 2θ=30–80°. The vacuum was reported as approximately 4.2×10^-6 atm overall pressure, with another section estimating p(O2)=8.82×10^-7 atm; oxygen partial pressure was not measured directly. Air tests used ambient atmosphere. Thermodynamic phase calculations covered 200–1600 °C, while oxide calculations at 1000 °C varied oxygen activity from 10^-14 to 1 atm under equilibrium assumptions.
generation.structural_mediator: Heating transformed the initial BCC/B2 substrate through FCC and Cr-Fe-rich sigma-phase formation at intermediate temperatures, followed by sigma dissolution at higher temperature. Oxidation generated an Al-rich external Al2O3 scale with a Cr-rich/Cr2O3 inner region; air produced a thick duplex scale and a pronounced Al-depleted, FCC/B2-denuded subsurface zone, whereas vacuum produced a much thinner scale and thin transformed subsurface layer.
generation.mechanism: Selective oxidation occurred primarily by outward diffusion of Al, and secondarily Cr, to react with oxygen. High oxygen availability accelerated scale growth and Al consumption, producing external Al2O3 over an inner Cr2O3-rich layer and driving Al depletion and phase transformation beneath the scale. Under low p(O2), slower oxidation kinetics limited scale growth. The alloy was assigned to the Group-III Giggins–Pettit regime because its high Al content supports a continuous external alumina scale.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the initial BCC/B2 alloy and to low-p(O2) exposure, heating in air was expected to produce earlier/more extensive oxidation, a thicker Al2O3/Cr2O3 scale, and stronger Al-depletion-induced subsurface transformation; vacuum exposure was expected to retain only a thin, predominantly alumina protective film. Heating was also expected to destabilize the initial BCC/B2 constitution at intermediate temperatures through FCC and sigma formation, with sigma disappearing near the highest temperatures.
generation.baseline: The baseline was the polished as-cast alloy at room temperature, consisting mainly of BCC and B2 phases with no thermally grown oxide scale. For the environmental comparison, low-p(O2)/vacuum exposure served as the lower-oxidation reference relative to atmospheric air.
generation.boundary: The phase and oxidation results apply to the studied arc-melted AlCrCoFeNi composition during the specified non-equilibrium heating cycle up to 1100 °C. The initial BCC/B2 phases were stable with no major detected change to about 500 °C; FCC appeared around 550–600 °C, sigma around 600–650 °C, and sigma diminished/disappeared around 950–1050 °C. Detectable oxidation became pronounced around 900–1000 °C and depended strongly on oxygen availability. Thermo-Calc results represent equilibrium and differed somewhat in transformation temperatures and phase fractions.

falsification_experiment.design: Temperature-resolved in situ HTXRD discriminated substrate and oxide phases and their onset/disappearance temperatures; SEM-BSE cross-sections and EDX point, line, and map analyses measured scale morphology, thickness, elemental partitioning, Al depletion, and subsurface phase changes. Thermo-Calc predictions provided an equilibrium comparison.
measurements: Temperature-resolved in situ HTXRD discriminated substrate and oxide phases and their onset/disappearance temperatures; SEM-BSE cross-sections and EDX point, line, and map analyses measured scale morphology, thickness, elemental partitioning, Al depletion, and subsurface phase changes. Thermo-Calc predictions provided an equilibrium comparison.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the predicted outcome is not observed relative to the baseline, the hypothesis is rejected.
